instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview), and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

observations.text: In Act 17:29 'imagination' is the devising of human thought: the divine being is not to be thought like an image formed by the art and design of man. It is the human faculty that plans and forms an object, here an idol.
In Pro 18:11 'imagination' is the rich man's own picture of his wealth: it stands in his mind as a high wall around a strong city. The verse sets what he pictures against what the wealth actually is.
In 1Cor 8:2 this code is the Greek conjunction in the clause 'if anyone imagines that he knows'; it joins the clauses and carries no sense of imagining, which the verb of G1380 carries.
observations.grounds: If anyone imagines that he knows something

observations.text: In 1Cor 8:2 'imagines' is a person holding a belief about himself, that he knows something; and the verse sets it against real knowing. It is a self-held opinion.
observations.grounds: If anyone imagines that he knows something

observations.text: In Psa 41:7 'imagine' is devising and planning evil: those who hate the psalmist whisper together and plan the worst against him. It is a thought turned toward harm, not an idle picture.
observations.grounds: they imagine the worst for me

observations.text: In 1Ti 6:5 'imagining' is holding the belief that godliness is a means of gain; the verse says it of people far from the truth. It is a belief taken as true, in the verse a mistaken one.
observations.grounds: imagining that godliness is a means

observations.text: In Rom 2:3 this code is the Greek conjunction in the question 'do you suppose'; it joins the clause and carries no sense of supposing, which the verb in the same question carries.
In Jam 4:5 'suppose' is the writer asking whether the readers think the Scripture speaks to no purpose; it is a question of what they take to be so.
observations.grounds: do you suppose it is to no purpose

observations.text: In Joh 21:25 and Jam 1:7 'suppose' is thinking something to be so: the writer's modest judgment of how many books the world could hold, and the doubter's expectation that he will receive from the Lord. In both it is a belief held without proof.
observations.grounds: must not suppose that he will receive

observations.text: In Luk 7:43 and Act 2:15 'suppose' is taking something to be so: Simon answers that he takes the larger debt to be the one forgiven, and Peter says the men are not drunk as the hearers assume. It is an answer or assumption that the verse then tests.
In Act 13:25 'suppose' is the surmising of the crowd about who John is; John asks what they take him to be and says he is not that one.
observations.grounds: What do you suppose that I am

observations.text: In Gen 18:28 to 18:32 'suppose' is the Hebrew particle of possibility, 'perhaps', with which Abraham puts each lower number of righteous to the Lord. It sets a case and carries no thinking of its own.

In 2Sa 13:32 and 2Sa 13:33 'suppose' is the verb of saying in the heart: Jonadab tells David not to conclude that all the king's sons are dead, since only Amnon is. It is a conclusion drawn in the mind, here a wrong one.

In Joh 11:31, Joh 20:15 and Act 27:13 'supposing' is assuming something to be so: the Jews assume Mary is going to the tomb, Mary assumes Jesus is the gardener, and the sailors assume they have their purpose. In the three verses the assumption is held without testing, and the verse then shows the case.
observations.grounds: Supposing him to be the gardener

observations.text: In Luk 2:44, Act 14:19 and Act 16:27 'supposing' is assuming a fact: that the boy is in the group, that Paul is dead, that the prisoners have escaped. Each is acted on at once, and each proves wrong or is turned aside in the verse or after it.
observations.grounds: supposing that the prisoners had escaped

observations.text: An assumption that an act then rests on: the parents take the boy to be in the company and travel a day, the mourners take Mary to be going to the tomb, Mary takes Jesus for the gardener, the crowd takes Paul to be dead, the jailer takes the prisoners to have escaped, and the sailors take their purpose to be gained. In each verse the supposing is a belief about a present fact, and what is done follows from it and meets the facts in the verse. Verses: Luk 2:44, Joh 11:31, Joh 20:15, Act 14:19, Act 16:27, Act 27:13.

A belief or opinion held or put to another: a man imagines he knows something, people are imagining that godliness is gain, Jonadab warns David not to conclude that all the sons are dead, Simon gives his judgment, the writer judges how many books the world could hold, the hearers are told they suppose wrongly about drunkenness, the crowd is asked what it supposes of John, the one who judges is asked whether he supposes he escapes, the doubter must not expect to receive, and the readers are asked whether they suppose the Scripture speaks to no purpose. The word is a view that the verse tests, corrects or leaves to the hearer. Verses: 1Cor 8:2, 1Ti 6:5, 2Sa 13:32, 2Sa 13:33, Luk 7:43, Joh 21:25, Act 2:15, Act 13:25, Rom 2:3, Jam 1:7, Jam 4:5.

A case put as a possibility: Abraham sets one lower number of righteous after another with 'suppose', and the prophet puts a case of a son who sees his father's sins. The words are Hebrew particles of perhaps and behold that introduce a hypothetical case and carry no thinking of their own. Verses: Gen 18:28, Gen 18:29, Gen 18:30, Gen 18:31, Gen 18:32, Eze 18:14.
Imagining as devising evil: those who hate the psalmist whisper together and plan the worst against him. The Hebrew verb is of reckoning and devising, here turned toward harm. Verses: Psa 41:7.
observations.grounds: to think, plan, esteem, calculate, invent

observations.text: The mind's own picture or device: in Pro 18:11 the rich man's wealth is a high wall in his imagination, a conceit that is not the fact, and in Act 17:29 the image of gold or stone is formed by human design and thought. The word is what the human mind pictures or devises. Verses: Pro 18:11, Act 17:29.

The codes of supposing a present fact are G1380 (to think, consider, regard; to think, imagine, suppose, presume) and G3543 (to think, suppose, expect; to suppose, presume, expect, with Luk 2:44 named). The lexicon bears out a belief taken up about what is so, on which the act in Luk 2:44, Joh 11:31, Joh 20:15, Act 14:19, Act 16:27 and Act 27:13 then rests.

The codes of a view held or put to another are G1380 (to think, imagine, suppose, presume), G3543 (to deem, with 1Ti 6:5 named), G3633 (to think, suppose, imagine, presume, with Joh 21:25 and Jam 1:7 named), G5274 (to take up a notion, suppose), G5282 (to suspect, suppose, deem, with Act 13:25 named) and H0559 (to say, to say in one's heart, to think) in 2Sa 13:32 and 2Sa 13:33. The lexicon bears out a view or opinion. G1161 (but, and, then) is a conjunction in the units of 1Cor 8:2 and Jam 4:5 and carries no thinking.

The codes of a case put as a possibility are H0194 (perhaps, peradventure; suppose) in Gen 18:28 to Gen 18:32 and H2009 (behold, lo, see, if) in Eze 18:14. The lexicon bears out particles that open a case and name no act of the mind.

The code of imagining harm is H2803I (to think, plan, devise, mean, invent), whose sense head is devise, plot, plan. The lexicon bears out the planning of the worst against the psalmist in Psa 41:7. H5921A (upon, against) is the preposition in the unit, naming against whom the plan is turned.

The codes of the mind's own picture are H4906 (show-piece, figure, image; imagination, conceit) in Pro 18:11 and G1761 (thought, reflection; the result of thought, invention, device, with Act 17:29 named) in Act 17:29. The lexicon bears out what the mind pictures or devises, a conceit in Pro 18:11 and a design in Act 17:29.

The surface imagination carries two codes: H4906 in Pro 18:11, a figure or conceit, where the rich man's wealth is a high wall in his own picture of it, and G1761 in Act 17:29, the result of thought, a device, where an image is formed by human art and design. Both are what the mind pictures or devises.
observations.grounds: like a high wall in his imagination

observations.text: The surface imagine in Psa 41:7 carries H2803I, to plan or devise, with H5921A, the preposition against: the haters devise the worst, and the preposition names the psalmist as the one it is turned against.
observations.grounds: they imagine the worst for me

observations.text: The surface imagines in 1Cor 8:2 carries G1380, to think or presume, with G1161, a conjunction that carries no thinking: the one who presumes he knows something is the subject.
observations.grounds: If anyone imagines that he knows something

observations.text: The surface suppose in Gen 18:28 to Gen 18:32 carries H0194, perhaps, and in Eze 18:14 H2009, behold: particles that open a case put as a possibility, with no act of the mind. Abraham names a lower number each time, and the prophet sets the case of a son.

The surface suppose in 2Sa 13:32, 2Sa 13:33, Luk 7:43, Joh 21:25, Act 2:15, Act 13:25, Rom 2:3, Jam 1:7 and Jam 4:5 is a view held or put to another: H0559 (to say in one's heart) in the two Samuel verses, G5274 in Luk 7:43 and Act 2:15, G3633 in Joh 21:25 and Jam 1:7, G5282 in Act 13:25, G1380 in Jam 4:5, and in Rom 2:3 G1161, a conjunction under which the English places the question.
observations.grounds: What do you suppose that I am

observations.text: The surface supposing carries G3543 in Luk 2:44, Act 14:19 and Act 16:27 and G1380 in Joh 11:31, Joh 20:15 and Act 27:13, both to think or suppose: in each a belief about a present fact is taken up and an act follows from it.
observations.grounds: supposing him to be the gardener

observations.text: Where suppose opens a case, the qualifiers are the numbers of the case and the answers to it: five short of fifty, forty, thirty, twenty, ten in Gen 18:28 to Gen 18:32, with there and again; the negators reach the Lord's answer (I will not destroy) and Abraham's plea that the Lord not be angry, not the supposing. In Eze 18:14 the negator reaches the son's not doing as his father did.

A negator reaches the supposing itself in 2Sa 13:32, 2Sa 13:33 and Jam 1:7: let not my lord suppose, must not suppose; the view is forbidden. In Act 2:15 and Act 13:25 the negator reaches what the view gets wrong (not drunk, I am not he), and in Act 17:29 the negator reaches the thinking that the divine being is like an image of human imagination.

In 1Cor 8:2 not and yet reach the knowing that the one who imagines lacks; in Jam 4:5 to no purpose is what the readers are asked whether they suppose of the Scripture; in Luk 7:43 larger names the debt in Simon's view and rightly is Jesus' verdict on it.

Where supposing is a belief an act rests on, the qualifiers describe the act or its setting, not the supposing: relatives and acquaintances where they search in Luk 2:44, quickly and there in Joh 11:31, where in Joh 20:15, woke in Act 16:27, along the shore in Act 27:13; in Joh 21:25 many other things are what the writer supposes the world could not hold, and in Pro 18:11 rich names the man whose wealth is a wall in his imagination.
observations.grounds: supposing him to be in the group

observations.text: In 2Sa 13:32 and 2Sa 13:33 Jonadab, son of Shimeah and brother of David, speaks to the king against a view: that all the young men, the king's sons, are dead. He names Amnon as the one dead, Absalom as the one who purposed it, and Tamar his sister as the cause.

In Joh 20:15 the woman Mary takes Jesus, who speaks to her, for the gardener: the one supposed about is Jesus himself. In Joh 21:25 the writer supposes about the many things Jesus did and the books they would fill.
observations.grounds: Supposing him to be the gardener

observations.text: Man and God are named together where the view is false or forbidden: in Act 17:29 God's offspring must not think the divine like an image of man's imagination, in Rom 2:3 the man who judges is asked whether he supposes he escapes God's judgment, in 1Ti 6:5 people depraved in mind imagine godliness is gain, and in Jam 1:7 the doubting person must not suppose he will receive from the Lord.
observations.grounds: an image formed by the art and imagination of man

observations.text: In 2Sa 13:32 and 2Sa 13:33 the view runs from the king toward a report about his sons, and Jonadab speaks from one person to another to turn it: the supposing is the king's, the correction is Jonadab's.
In Joh 20:15 the supposing runs from Mary toward the one in front of her: she takes Jesus for the gardener while he speaks to her.
observations.grounds: Supposing him to be the gardener
